ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a section of transmission line whose characteristic impedance is labeled Z0, with a short-circuited stub connected in parallel at the junction on the left side; the main transmission line extends from this junction to the right to the load ZL=100 Ω, and the figure marks the length from the junction to the load as λ/2. The length of the stub is labeled λ/8, and it is short-circuited at the end. The problem gives Z0=50 Ω. Reasoning: The total admittance seen at the junction is the sum of the two parallel admittances: the main-line input admittance and the short-circuited-stub input admittance. Since the main-line segment has length λ/2, the load impedance repeats its original value after being transformed through λ/2 on a lossless transmission line, so the main-line input impedance is 100 Ω, and the main-line input admittance is Y_line=1/100=0.01 mho. The short-circuited stub length is λ/8, therefore βl=2π/λ · λ/8=π/4; the short-circuited-stub input admittance is Y_stub=-jY0 cot(βl), where Y0=1/Z0=1/50=0.02 mho, cot(π/4)=1, so Y_stub=-j0.02 mho. Adding the two gives Y=Y_line+Y_stub=0.01-j0.02 mho.

Compute the shorted stub admittance using its \(\lambda/8\) length and \(Z_0=50\,\Omega\): \(Y_{stub}=-jY_0\cot(\pi/4)=-j0.02\) mho. Sum them to get \(Y=0.01-j0.02\) mho.

method.method_draft: Normalize all admittances to \(Y_0=1/50=0.02\) S. The load branch has \(z_L=100/50=2\), so after a \(\lambda/2\) rotation it remains \(z=2\), giving normalized admittance \(y_{line}=1/2=0.5\). For the shorted shunt stub, start at the short-circuit point and move \(\lambda/8\) toward the junction on the admittance chart; this gives normalized stub admittance \(y_{stub}=-j1\). Add normalized shunt admittances: \(y=0.5-j1\). Denormalize: \(Y=(0.5-j1)(0.02)=0.01-j0.02\) mho.
